name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Manual runs: re-checking a branch against a moved main, or confirming a gate after
  # changing one, without pushing an empty commit.
  workflow_dispatch:
  # An advisory published after a merge is invisible until someone opens a pull request, and this
  # repository can go days without one. Monday 07:00 UTC; only `build-chain` answers it.
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'

# Every job here only reads the checkout; the repo default is write.
permissions:
  contents: read

# A newer push to the same branch supersedes an in-flight run. main is exempt:
# every commit there should have its own recorded result.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify
    # The scheduled run exists for the dependency audit; re-running the suite on an unchanged
    # tree every Monday would report nothing new.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Full history, not for this job but for the spec anchor check below:
          # it resolves cited content from
          # origin/main, which a shallow clone cannot serve.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      # --ignore-scripts so `prepare` does not build on install: what a lifecycle script
      # runs is out of this workflow's control, and the Build step below is where a broken
      # compile should be reported. Type check catches it earlier still.
      - name: Install
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # Every `npm run` step below is one link of the `verify` script in
      # package.json, in the same order - scripts/verify-script.test.ts holds
      # the two together - and kept as separate steps so a red run names the
      # gate that failed rather than a single opaque command.
      - name: Type check
        run: npm run typecheck

      # example/ is outside tsconfig.json's rootDir, so nothing checked the one
      # file the README and the guide are written against.
      - name: Type check the example
        run: npm run typecheck:example

      - name: Lint (--max-warnings 0)
        run: npm run eslint

      # Reports, never blocks. The one rule it runs is `warn`, so the step exits
      # 0 on its own and carries no continue-on-error: a non-zero exit here now
      # means the config itself broke, and that should fail. Its findings render
      # as warning annotations rather than failures, which is what a report on a
      # passing check should look like.
      #
      # require-statement-links counts spec statements with no test behind them.
      # Most of what it reports needs a test written rather than a line changed,
      # so the count is meant to be visible on every run and to fall over time.
      # Its test-side mirror, require-spec-link, is satisfied and gates in the
      # Lint step above. Never add a rule here to escape a red gate -
      # eslint.config.backlog.mjs says what belongs.
      - name: Spec traceability backlog (report)
        run: npm run lint:backlog

      - name: Format check
        run: npm run prettier:check

      # Runs the whole suite and fails it on the committed coverage floor in
      # jest.config.js, so this is the test gate rather than an extra pass.
      - name: Test (with coverage floor)
        run: npm run test:coverage

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      # Anchors drift silently: a cited file gaining or losing lines above the
      # cited one leaves the link pointing at different content, and the spec
      # still reads as cited. Resolves content at origin/main, which the
      # fetch-depth: 0 above exists to provide. A red check is fixed by running
      # `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` and committing the result.
      - name: Spec anchor check
        run: node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main

      # A citation counts as coverage only in its statement's trailing
      # parenthetical; one written mid-statement is dropped by the Lore job in silence,
      # so the spec reads as cited while its coverage is zero. A red check is
      # fixed by moving the link to the end of its statement, never by deleting
      # it (AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links).
      # Every fenced typescript block in the three documented files is generated
      # from source; hand transcription is what produced the defects this catches.
      - name: Documented code blocks
        run: npm run docs:check

      # Three rules that held only because somebody remembered them: a path in prose that resolves,
      # a spike that says it is a spike, and an example region inside the EU.
      - name: Documented paths resolve
        run: npm run docs:check-paths

      - name: Spike documents carry a status block
        run: npm run docs:check-spikes

      - name: Documented regions
        run: npm run check:regions

      # A line number is a derived pointer; the name is what the author cited. This catches a citation
      # whose line moved under it, which no baseline comparison can see on a branch that edits the spec.
      - name: Spec citations name their test
        run: npm run spec:names

      - name: Spec link placement
        run: npm run check:spec-links

      # Lead paragraphs and a spec's status-vs-coverage are ESLint's job; the
      # one verdict a `files` glob cannot express - that an ADR's frontmatter
      # status parses, without holding the ADR to the coverage tier - is this
      # script's. `check:spec-status -- --coverage` lists unlinked statements
      # and never gates.
      - name: Spec status
        run: npm run check:spec-status

      # A release note and a commit subject have different readers, so this is a
      # file the author writes rather than something derived from the log. The
      # label is the escape hatch for a src/ change nothing installable observes.
      - name: Changelog entry
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'no-changelog')
        # No fetch: the checkout above resolves every head into refs/remotes
        # with fetch-depth 0, and its credential is gone by the time a step
        # runs, so fetching here asked an unauthenticated git for a private
        # repository and exited 128 before the gate was ever reached.
        run: bash scripts/check-changelog.sh "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"

  # Separate job, not a step on `verify`: these two check what the build chain
  # pulls in rather than what the code does, and a red audit should not read as
  # a failing test suite. It needs the tree installed but nothing built, so it
  # skips `prepare` with --ignore-scripts.
  build-chain:
    name: Build chain
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install (no build)
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # Full tree, dev included: those packages are what a runner installs
      # before building dist/, and the release workflow signs what it produces.
      - name: Audit (high and above)
        run: npm run check:audit

      # A tag is a mutable pointer its owner can repoint under a job that holds
      # repository credentials.
      - name: Action pins
        run: npm run check:action-pins

  # devDependencies pins driver 7, so every other job tests 7 alone; this one
  # keeps 6, the other half of the peer range, tested.
  mongo-driver-6:
    name: Mongo driver 6
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install (no build)
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      - name: Swap in driver 6
        run: npm install --no-save --ignore-scripts mongodb@6

name: Guard main pushes

# The alarm for a commit that reaches main without a pull request.
#
# Branch protection is the lock; this is the smoke detector behind it. The
# pattern it watches for is a real one this org has already been hit by
# (re-cinq/lore#1062): a stolen token pushed commits straight to an unprotected
# main, authored as github-actions[bot], with no PR anywhere.
#
# It matters more here than in a service repo. publish.yml fires on `v*` tags
# and authenticates to npm through OIDC trusted publishing with no stored
# secret to revoke - so push access to main is, transitively, the ability to
# publish @re-cinq/bowman-ui as this org.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  guard:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Flag commits on main with no associated PR
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          BEFORE: ${{ github.event.before }}
          AFTER: ${{ github.event.after }}
          PUSHER: ${{ github.actor }}
          CREATED: ${{ github.event.created }}
          COMMIT_IDS: ${{ toJson(github.event.commits.*.id) }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # Branch creation carries no meaningful before-state to diff against.
          if [ "$CREATED" = "true" ]; then
            echo "main was just created - nothing to compare."
            exit 0
          fi

          # A commit that arrived via a merged PR resolves to that PR here; one
          # pushed directly resolves to none. An API error must count as "no PR"
          # (fail closed): gh prints the raw error body to stdout, so trusting
          # captured output would wave a commit through on any 4xx/5xx.
          pr_count_for() {
            local count
            if ! count=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$1/pulls" --jq 'length'); then
              echo "PR lookup for $1 failed - treating as no PR" >&2
              echo 0
              return
            fi
            case "$count" in
              '' | *[!0-9]*) echo 0 ;;
              *) echo "$count" ;;
            esac
          }

          # The commit-to-PR index is eventually consistent: a squash-merge
          # queried seconds after landing can still resolve to no PR. Re-check
          # the unresolved set for up to 45s before flagging. Retrying the set
          # rather than each commit bounds total sleep regardless of push size.
          pending=$(echo "$COMMIT_IDS" | jq -r '.[]')
          for pass in 1 2 3 4; do
            unresolved=""
            # Unquoted on purpose: word-splitting the newline-separated shas is
            # the iteration mechanism.
            for sha in $pending; do
              if [ "$(pr_count_for "$sha")" = "0" ]; then
                unresolved="${unresolved}${sha}"$'\n'
              fi
            done
            pending="$unresolved"
            [ -z "$pending" ] && break
            if [ "$pass" -lt 4 ]; then
              echo "Commit(s) still resolving to no PR after pass $pass, retrying in 15s..."
              sleep 15
            fi
          done

          if [ -z "$pending" ]; then
            echo "All pushed commits trace to a PR - OK."
            exit 0
          fi

          suspicious=""
          for sha in $pending; do
            if ! author=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$sha" \
              --jq '.author.login // .commit.author.name // "unknown"' 2>/dev/null); then
              author=unknown
            fi
            echo "::warning title=Direct push to main::$sha by $author has no associated PR"
            suspicious="${suspicious}- \`${sha}\` - author \`${author}\`, no associated PR"$'\n'
          done

          title="Direct/unattributed push to main: ${AFTER:0:12}"
          body=$(printf 'Push by `%s` to `main` (`%s`..`%s`) contains commit(s) with **no associated pull request** - a direct push or an unattributed bot commit.\n\n%s\nThis repo publishes to npm from a `v*` tag via OIDC trusted publishing, so push access to `main` is transitively publish access.\n\nIf this was an intentional admin action, close this issue. Otherwise investigate immediately, treat every reachable credential as exposed, and rotate.' "$PUSHER" "${BEFORE:0:12}" "${AFTER:0:12}" "$suspicious")
          gh label create security --repo "$REPO" --color D93F0B --description "Security" 2>/dev/null || true
          # The alarm must fire even when the label is unavailable: fall back to
          # an unlabeled issue rather than dying on "'security' not found".
          gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --label security --title "$title" --body "$body" \
            || gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --body "$body"
          # Loud on every channel: the issue is the durable alarm, the red check
          # is the visible one.
          exit 1

# The alarm for a commit that reaches main without a pull request.
#
# Branch protection is the lock; this is the detector behind it. A rule can be
# relaxed, a ruleset can be replaced, and a token with push access is not bound
# by either - none of which leaves a trace of its own.
#
# It matters in this repository specifically because publish.yml fires on a v*
# tag and authenticates to npm through OIDC trusted publishing, with no stored
# secret to revoke. Push access to main is transitively the right to publish
# under the @re-cinq scope.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Flag commits with no pull request
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # The range below needs the graph on both sides of the push.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Flag commits on main with no associated pull request
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          BEFORE: ${{ github.event.before }}
          AFTER: ${{ github.event.after }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          # The null sha means main had no previous tip this runner can see (a
          # first push, or a force-push past it). Judge the new tip alone rather
          # than walking the whole history and filing an issue per commit.
          if [ "${BEFORE}" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ] || ! git cat-file -e "${BEFORE}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::no usable previous tip (${BEFORE}); checking ${AFTER} alone"
            COMMITS="${AFTER}"
          else
            COMMITS=$(git rev-list "${BEFORE}..${AFTER}")
          fi

          # The repo has no `security` label; create it once rather than let
          # every issue fall back to none.
          gh label create security --color B60205 --description "Vulnerability or credential exposure" 2>/dev/null || true

          FLAGGED=0
          for SHA in ${COMMITS}; do
            # A PR merge associates every commit it carried, so a normal merge
            # reports nothing here. An empty array is the whole finding.

            # The association is by sha, so a rewritten commit loses it - this
            # repo's pre-rewrite history reports 0 for commits that did have a
            # PR. Harmless: the range above only judges what this push added.
            COUNT=$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/commits/${SHA}/pulls" --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo "error")
            if [ "${COUNT}" = "error" ]; then
              echo "::warning::could not resolve pull requests for ${SHA}; not flagging it"
              continue
            fi
            if [ "${COUNT}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "ok ${SHA} (${COUNT} pull request(s))"
              continue
            fi

            TITLE="Commit ${SHA} reached main with no pull request"
            # Re-running this workflow on the same push must not file it twice.
            if [ -n "$(gh issue list --state all --search "${SHA} in:title" --json number --jq '.[0].number' 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
              echo "already filed for ${SHA}"
              continue
            fi

            # Commit metadata reaches the body through a file, never through the
            # shell: a subject line is attacker-controlled text.
            {
              echo "\`${SHA}\` is on \`main\` and the pull requests API associates it with none."
              echo
              echo "| Field | Value |"
              echo "| --- | --- |"
              printf '| Author | %s |\n' "$(git log -1 --format='%an <%ae>' "${SHA}" | tr -d '|')"
              printf '| Committer | %s |\n' "$(git log -1 --format='%cn <%ce>' "${SHA}" | tr -d '|')"
              printf '| Committed | %s |\n' "$(git log -1 --format='%cI' "${SHA}")"
              echo
              echo "Subject:"
              echo
              echo '```'
              git log -1 --format='%s' "${SHA}"
              echo '```'
              echo
              echo "Branch protection requires a pull request, so this is either a protection change, a"
              echo "bypass, or a token pushing directly. Push access to \`main\` is transitively the right"
              echo "to publish this package, so treat it as a credential question until shown otherwise."
              echo
              echo "Detected by [this run](${RUN_URL})."
            } > body.md

            gh issue create --title "${TITLE}" --body-file body.md --label security >/dev/null \
              || gh issue create --title "${TITLE}" --body-file body.md >/dev/null
            echo "::error::${TITLE}"
            FLAGGED=$((FLAGGED + 1))
          done

          echo "checked $(echo "${COMMITS}" | wc -w) commit(s), flagged ${FLAGGED}"
          # The issue is the deliverable, not a red run: failing here would also
          # fail the push that merged a legitimate pull request.
          exit 0

## The release pipeline

### Coverage floor

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs typecheck, lint, the traceability backlog report, format, test, build, and three spec-consistency checks. It does not measure coverage.

- `jest.config.js` gains `collectCoverageFrom` and `coverageThreshold`, and `package.json` gains a `test:coverage` script. CI's existing `Test` step calls it instead of `npm test`, so the floor gates the suite rather than adding a second full run.
- Coverage is collected from `src/` only. The `scripts/` suites drive their subjects through `spawnSync`, so an instrumented `.mjs` would report zero however well it is tested. `providerTestSupport.ts` is excluded as test scaffolding rather than shipped source.
- The floor is set at the measured baseline, not an aspiration, and exactly at it rather than rounded down: an integer floor leaves roughly a percent of slack, which was measured to let four untested lines through without failing.
- Measured at `3186f07` with those exclusions: 67.96% statements, 57.54% branches, 68% functions, 68.34% lines, across 206 tests in 17 suites. The earlier figure of 61.32% lines predates the exclusions and three of this branch's commits.
- The floor is a ratchet: a change that lowers coverage fails the job and is fixed by adding the missing test, never by lowering the number; a change that raises coverage should raise the floor with it.
- `coverage/` is gitignored already, so nothing is added for it.

### Build-chain audit

AGENTS.md § Quality Gates already commits this repository to "npm audit must show no vulnerabilities", and nothing enforced it. Measured before this work: 18 advisories — 1 critical, 6 high, 8 moderate, 3 low — and `ws`, a direct production dependency, was one of the six high.

- A check fails on any unacknowledged advisory at `high` or above, over the full installed tree rather than production dependencies only. The dev tree is what a runner installs before building `dist/`, and after the release workflow exists that runner holds `id-token: write`.
- Acceptances live in `.github/audit-acknowledgements.json`, one entry per advisory, each naming the advisory, the package, the reason, an ISO expiry and who accepted it. An entry that is expired, malformed, or matches no current advisory fails the check too — a stale acceptance is a claim nobody has rechecked.
- A second check fails when any `uses:` reference under `.github/` is not a 40-character commit SHA, skipping `./` and `docker://` references, which cannot be pinned that way. Every reference was tag-pinned when this was written and is now SHA-pinned with the tag kept in a trailing comment.
- Both checks run as their own CI job rather than as steps on the existing one, because they report on what the build chain pulls in rather than on what the code does, and again before `npm publish`.
- `npm audit fix` clears the backlog to 3 advisories — 2 moderate, 1 low, none at high or above — touching only `package-lock.json`. No dependency range in `package.json` changes, and the suite passes unchanged, so no acceptance entry is needed to go green.

Importing a package is not installing it. A smoke test that needs killing is hiding a leaked handle from every consumer, which the engine's unreferenced heartbeat timer once was. Proved by leaking a handle deliberately and watching the runner refuse it.
- The consumer directory is asserted to be outside the repository rather than assumed to be: `mktemp` honours `TMPDIR`, and a `TMPDIR` inside the tree would quietly restore the resolution the whole script exists to prevent.

Two variants, because a consumer is in one of two states and they fail differently.

- `bare` installs neither optional peer — a mock-provider consumer. It asserts both peers are absent, runs the engine, and type-checks.
- `full` installs both at the versions `peerDependencies` names, and asserts both providers construct with their SDK loaded. Nothing here holds cloud credentials, so construction is the whole assertion; a call would fail for reasons that say nothing about this package.
- Neither variant is advisory. `bare` proves an absent peer fails well, `full` proves a present one is reached, and a provider that is dead on arrival passes the first and fails the second.
- The type check runs under `moduleResolution: "nodenext"` and again under `"bundler"`. NodeNext reads `exports.types` through the node condition; `bundler` is what a Next.js consumer uses and resolves differently, and a package can satisfy one and not the other.

### Release workflow

The repository has zero git tags. `0.1.0` was never tagged and never published, so there is no existing convention to fit around.

- Publishing a GitHub Release triggers one publish job. The release carries the tag and the notes; the version is the one already committed in `package.json`, so a release names a version a pull request agreed to rather than minting one at the point of no return. A draft release fires nothing, and one ticked as a pre-release is refused by the job condition before a runner starts.
- `workflow_dispatch` exists for one case: re-running a publish that failed after the release already exists. The earlier objection to it - that a publish startable by hand takes whatever branch somebody picks in a dropdown - is answered by the guards rather than by removing the trigger. The version guard reads the ref name and refuses anything that is not a `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` tag, and the ancestry check refuses a commit that is not on `main`, so a branch chosen there fails closed. The one exception is the single-use bootstrap under § First publish, which is a separate workflow file, runs once, and is deleted in the same change that registers the trusted publisher.
- Prereleases are refused rather than routed to a dist-tag, twice over: the job condition refuses a release ticked as a pre-release, and the version guard refuses the tag shape. name: Publish images

# Build and push the controller and agent runtime images to GHCR. On main this runs
# only after the CI workflow succeeds on the merged commit (workflow_run gate), so a
# red build never produces a signed image; version tags and manual dispatch publish
# directly. The agent image is the AGENT_IMAGE the controller injects as each run
# pod's init container; the controller image backs deploy/controller.yaml.
#
# Multi-arch: each image is built natively for linux/amd64 (ubuntu-latest) and
# linux/arm64 (ubuntu-24.04-arm, free for public repos) — no QEMU, which would
# make the LDC compile ~10x slower and flaky. Each leg pushes an untagged image by
# digest; the `merge` job stitches the legs into one OCI index per image, applies
# the tags, and signs the index. That index digest is the one pinned and verified.
#
# Supply chain: each pushed image is signed with cosign (keyless, via the GitHub
# OIDC token — no stored keys) and carries an SPDX SBOM + SLSA provenance
# attestation per platform. The immutable digest is written to the run summary.
#
# Releases: on a v* tag the `release` job renders deploy/ to a single digest-pinned
# install.yaml and attaches it to the GitHub Release — the published `kubectl apply
# -f` artifact, and pushes the cosign-signed Helm chart packaged from the same
# checkout to oci://ghcr.io/re-cinq/charts. The `pin` job then opens a PR that points deploy/ AND the docs
# cosign-verify example at the same digests (scripts/pin-image-digests.sh), so main
# never ships a floating :latest. See README "Releases".

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
  push:
    tags: ['v*']
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write
  id-token: write # keyless cosign signing via the GitHub OIDC token

jobs:
  build:
    # On main, only publish if the CI workflow that triggered us passed AND it ran
    # on this repo's own main branch — a fork PR's CI also emits a workflow_run
    # whose head_branch is the fork's branch name, so without the head_repository
    # guard a fork that names its branch "main" could get its commit built, pushed
    # to GHCR, and cosign-signed with our OIDC identity. Tag releases and manual
    # dispatch (no workflow_run context) always run.
    if: >-
      ${{ github.event_name != 'workflow_run' ||
          (github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
           github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository &&
           github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main') }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.platform.os }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        image:
          - name: ghcr.io/re-cinq/ai-agent-controller
            file: deploy/Dockerfile.controller
            key: controller
          - name: ghcr.io/re-cinq/ai-agent
            file: scripts/container/Dockerfile.agent
            key: agent
        platform:
          - { os: ubuntu-latest, target: linux/amd64, arch: amd64 }
          - { os: ubuntu-24.04-arm, target: linux/arm64, arch: arm64 }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          # On the workflow_run path, build the exact commit CI validated; otherwise
          # the tag / dispatch ref.
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
      # docker-container driver — the runner's default `docker` driver can't emit
      # the SBOM/provenance attestations the build step requests below.
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@8d2750c68a42422c14e847fe6c8ac0403b4cbd6f # v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@c94ce9fb468520275223c153574b00df6fe4bcc9 # v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@c299e40c65443455700f0fdfc63efafe5b349051 # v5
        with:
          images: ${{ matrix.image.name }}
      # Untagged, pushed by digest only; the merge job applies the tags to the index.
      - id: build
        uses: docker/build-push-action@10e90e3645eae34f1e60eeb005ba3a3d33f178e8 # v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: ${{ matrix.image.file }}
          platforms: ${{ matrix.platform.target }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          outputs: type=image,name=${{ matrix.image.name }},push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=true
          sbom: true # SPDX SBOM attestation, attached to the image
          provenance: mode=max # SLSA build provenance attestation
      # Hand each leg's digest to the merge job. A matrix can't set distinct
      # job outputs (legs share one map, last writer wins), so go via artifacts.
      - name: Stage the platform digest for the merge job
        env:
          DIGEST: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
        run: echo "${DIGEST}" > "${{ matrix.platform.arch }}.digest"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: leg-${{ matrix.image.key }}-${{ matrix.platform.arch }}
          path: ${{ matrix.platform.arch }}.digest
          retention-days: 1

  # Stitch the per-platform images into one tagged OCI index per image and sign
  # it. `imagetools create` carries each leg's SBOM/provenance manifests into the
  # index; `cosign sign --recursive` signs the index AND the per-platform
  # manifests, so verifying a platform-resolved digest also passes.
  merge:
    name: Merge platforms and sign
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - image: ghcr.io/re-cinq/ai-agent-controller
            key: controller
          - image: ghcr.io/re-cinq/ai-agent
            key: agent
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4
        with:
          pattern: leg-${{ matrix.key }}-*
          path: legs
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@8d2750c68a42422c14e847fe6c8ac0403b4cbd6f # v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@c94ce9fb468520275223c153574b00df6fe4bcc9 # v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@c299e40c65443455700f0fdfc63efafe5b349051 # v5
        with:
          images: ${{ matrix.image }}
          tags: |
            type=raw,value=latest,enable={{is_default_branch}}
            type=ref,event=tag
            type=sha
      - id: index
        name: Create the multi-arch index
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ matrix.image }}
          META_JSON: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.json }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tag_args="$(jq -r '.tags[] | "-t \(.)"' <<<"${META_JSON}")"
          first_tag="$(jq -r '.tags[0]' <<<"${META_JSON}")"
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # tag_args is a deliberate word list
          docker buildx imagetools create ${tag_args} \
            "${IMAGE}@$(cat legs/amd64.digest)" \
            "${IMAGE}@$(cat legs/arm64.digest)"
          digest="$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "${first_tag}" --format '{{.Manifest.Digest}}')"
          echo "digest=${digest}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@398d4b0eeef1380460a10c8013a76f728fb906ac # v3
      - name: Sign the index and its platform manifests by digest (keyless)
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ matrix.image }}
          DIGEST: ${{ steps.index.outputs.digest }}
        run: cosign sign --yes --recursive "${IMAGE}@${DIGEST}"
      - name: Record the immutable digest
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ matrix.image }}
          DIGEST: ${{ steps.index.outputs.digest }}
        run: echo "- \`${IMAGE}@${DIGEST}\` (linux/amd64, linux/arm64)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      # Hand the index digest to the release and pin jobs (artifacts again, same
      # matrix-output limitation as above).
      - name: Stage the digest for the pin job
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        env:
          DIGEST: ${{ steps.index.outputs.digest }}
        run: echo "${DIGEST}" > "${{ matrix.key }}.digest"
      - name: Upload the digest
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: digest-${{ matrix.key }}
          path: ${{ matrix.key }}.digest
          retention-days: 1

  # On a v* tag, render the tagged deploy/ to one flat, digest-pinned install.yaml
  # and attach it to the GitHub Release. This is the artifact `kubectl apply -f
  # .../releases/.../install.yaml` fetches. The digests come from the build outputs
  # above (no registry read). The pin script also rewrites the docs cosign example
  # here, but only deploy/ feeds `kubectl kustomize` and this checkout is discarded.
  #
  # The same pinned checkout is packaged as the Helm chart (deploy/helm, ADR-004),
  # pushed to oci://ghcr.io/re-cinq/charts, cosign-signed by its pushed digest like
  # the images, and attached to the release next to install.yaml.
  release:
    name: Render and attach install.yaml and the Helm chart
    needs: merge
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write # create the release and upload the assets
      packages: write # push the chart to ghcr.io/re-cinq/charts
      id-token: write # keyless cosign signing of the chart
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6 # the tagged commit, so install.yaml matches the release
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4
        with:
          pattern: digest-*
          path: digests
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: azure/setup-kubectl@776406bce94f63e41d621b960d78ee25c8b76ede # v4 # provides `kubectl kustomize`
      - name: Render the digest-pinned install.yaml
        env:
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          export CONTROLLER_DIGEST="$(cat digests/controller.digest)"
          export AGENT_DIGEST="$(cat digests/agent.digest)"
          ./scripts/pin-image-digests.sh "$TAG"
          kubectl kustomize deploy > install.yaml
      - uses: azure/setup-helm@9bc31f4ebc9c6b171d7bfbaa5d006ae7abdb4310 # v5.0.1
        with:
          version: v3.19.0
      - uses: docker/login-action@c94ce9fb468520275223c153574b00df6fe4bcc9 # v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - id: chart
        name: Package and push the Helm chart
        env:
          ACTOR: ${{ github.actor }}
          REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          helm registry login ghcr.io --username "$ACTOR" --password-stdin <<<"$REGISTRY_TOKEN"
          package="$(helm package deploy/helm/ai-agent-subsystem | sed -n 's/^Successfully packaged chart and saved it to: //p')"
          digest="$(helm push "$package" oci://ghcr.io/re-cinq/charts 2>&1 | tee /dev/stderr | sed -n 's/^Digest: //p')"
          echo "package=${package}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "digest=${digest}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@398d4b0eeef1380460a10c8013a76f728fb906ac # v3
      - name: Sign the chart by digest (keyless)
        env:
          DIGEST: ${{ steps.chart.outputs.digest }}
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes "ghcr.io/re-cinq/charts/ai-agent-subsystem@${DIGEST}"
          echo "- \`ghcr.io/re-cinq/charts/ai-agent-subsystem@${DIGEST}\` (Helm chart)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
      - name: Create or update the release and upload install.yaml and the chart
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          CHART: ${{ steps.chart.outputs.package }}
        run: |
          # A hyphen marks a semver pre-release (v0.1.0-rc1); flag it so it never
          # becomes the "latest" release that releases/latest/download/ serves.
          prerelease=""
          case "$TAG" in *-*) prerelease="--prerelease";; esac
          gh release create "$TAG" install.yaml "$CHART" --generate-notes $prerelease \
            || gh release upload "$TAG" install.yaml "$CHART" --clobber

  # On a v* tag, point deploy/ at the exact signed digests this run built and open
  # a PR. The digests come from the build outputs above, so no registry read is
  # needed. Requires the repo setting "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve
  # pull requests" (Settings -> Actions -> General). The PR is opened with the
  # default token, so it deliberately carries a digest-only change (deploy/ + the
  # docs cosign example) for a human to review and merge.
  pin:
    name: Pin deploy/ and docs to released digests
    needs: merge
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write # push the pin branch
      pull-requests: write # open the pin PR
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          ref: main # pin onto the development branch, not the tagged commit
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4
        with:
          pattern: digest-*
          path: digests
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Pin deploy/ + docs and open a PR
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          DOCS: website/src/content/docs/setup/install.md
        run: |
          export CONTROLLER_DIGEST="$(cat digests/controller.digest)"
          export AGENT_DIGEST="$(cat digests/agent.digest)"
          ./scripts/pin-image-digests.sh "$TAG"
          if git diff --quiet -- deploy/ "$DOCS"; then
            echo "deploy/ and docs already pinned to ${TAG}; nothing to do"
            exit 0
          fi
          branch="chore/pin-deploy-${TAG}"
          git config user.name  "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git switch -c "$branch"
          git commit -am "chore(release): pin deploy/ and docs to ${TAG} image digests"
          git push -u origin "$branch" --force-with-lease
          gh pr create --base main --head "$branch" \
            --title "chore(release): pin deploy/ and docs to ${TAG} image digests" \
            --body "Automated by the release pin job. deploy/ and the install-page cosign-verify example now reference the cosign-signed digests built for \`${TAG}\` instead of a mutable tag, closing the floating-\`:latest\` gap for this release."
